title: Git Diff for Human Reasoning

content_html:
Every investigation eventually reaches the same moment.

Two competent people look at the same evidence and walk away believing different things.

That isn't unusual. What's unusual is what happens next. We compare their conclusions. Not their reasoning. We argue over who is right. We almost never ask where they first began thinking differently.

That struck me as backwards.

We archive evidence. We rarely archive reasoning.

Every investigation leaves behind artifacts. Logs. Disk images. Photographs. Witness statements. Source code. Those artifacts become part of the permanent record, indexed, hashed, preserved for years.

Ironically, the reasoning that connected them usually disappears. The assumptions made along the way. The alternative explanations that were considered and rejected. The moment someone's confidence changed. Those things typically survive only in memory, in scattered notes, or in a conversation that was never written down at all.

Weeks later, someone reviewing the investigation may have every piece of evidence the original investigator had — and almost none of the analytical path that made those pieces meaningful. When disagreement shows up, we reconstruct the reasoning after the fact instead of inspecting reasoning that was recorded as it happened.

I began wondering whether that missing artifact — the reasoning itself was worth preserving. Not because it determines the truth. Because it explains how the truth was pursued.

We preserve evidence remarkably well. We preserve reasoning remarkably poorly.

Every investigator leaves fingerprints

Every investigator develops habits. Not bad habits, thinking habits.

Some build a timeline first, before anything else. Some distrust timelines on instinct, because clocks drift and nobody double-checks them. Some constantly ask, "what evidence would change my mind?" Others ask, "what explains the most observations?" Some investigators are naturally skeptical of a source until it survives repeated scrutiny. Others are naturally generative — they build a hypothesis fast and spend the rest of the investigation trying to break it.

Neither approach is wrong. They're different. And that's exactly why an investigation benefits from more than one independent person working it. If everyone followed the exact same process, they'd likely miss the exact same blind spots. Independent thinking isn't noise to eliminate. It's information to preserve.

The problem was never that investigators think differently. The problem is that we usually throw away the record of how they thought differently. By the time an investigation is written up, most of that path has disappeared into a polished narrative. The report tells you where they arrived. It rarely tells you the route they took.

I started wondering if the route was actually the interesting part.

What if we could diff reasoning the way Git diffs code?

Nobody reviews two versions of a file by reading each one top to bottom and holding the difference in their head. A diff tool does that reconstruction for you, it doesn't tell you which version is better, it just shows you exactly where and how they parted ways.

When two investigators disagree, we still tend to do it the old way: put both reports side by side and ask a third person to reconstruct where the thinking diverged. That reconstruction is slow, it's subjective, and it's usually incomplete, because neither analyst ever recorded their reasoning in a form that could actually be compared.

This does not mean nobody has tried to structure or preserve reasoning before. Structured analytic techniques, argument-mapping systems, and analytic-provenance tools have been doing parts of this work for years. I could not find a practical workflow centered specifically on freezing two independently authored reasoning paths, asking a separate reviewer to align them, and preserving those alignment decisions as part of the resulting diff. That narrower combination is what Reasoning Diff Lab is testing. A full treatment of the prior art, SEAS, CISpaces, W3C PROV, argument mapping, and the analytic-provenance literature is in the research assessment linked at the end.

So I built enough of an answer to find out whether the question was worth asking. I called it Reasoning Diff Lab.

Status: pilot-ready, empirically unvalidated. The current v2.0.0 release includes the analyst-entry workflow, frozen path snapshots, reviewer alignment, deterministic comparison reports, and three synthetic cases. It passes 58 tests with 0 failures, and a full build produces 22 divergence events across those cases. That proves the instrument runs as designed. It does not prove that investigators will find it useful that is exactly what the pilot below is designed to determine.

What it actually is

It's a local-first research prototype that compares two independently produced reasoning paths against the same evidence set.

I want to be just as clear about what it doesn't do, because this is the part that matters most. It does not determine truth, rank investigators, or declare one analyst better than the other. It does not infer a contradiction from wording a contradiction only exists in its output if a human reviewer explicitly confirms one. It does not replace human review; it tries to make that review faster to start, and harder to skip a step in.

Each analyst breaks their reasoning into small typed pieces an observation, an assumption, an inference, a claim, an explicit unknown and tags which evidence and which earlier piece each one depends on, with a confidence level attached. A reviewer who authored neither path matches the two sets: same position, related but distinct, or unrelated. Contradiction is separate it must be declared by the reviewer and is never guessed by the system. From there, everything is mechanical: the tool walks the matched and unmatched pieces and reports what it finds. If the report says two analysts diverged, you can trace that line back to the exact evidence, the exact dependency chain, and the exact reviewer decision whose call it was, and what they chose that produced it.

What it surfaces in practice:

  • Shared evidence, different interpretation. Both analysts cite the same authentication log. One reads it as stolen credentials. The other reads it as expired-token behavior. Same source, materially different explanation.
  • Evidence used by only one side. One analyst built part of their case on the deployment timeline. The other never touched it — maybe for a good reason, maybe because they never saw it.
  • Confidence divergence. Two analysts land on the same conclusion. One is 90% sure. The other is 55%. That gap is invisible if all you ever compare is the final sentence.
  • Undeclared support. A claim exists with no evidence and no stated reasoning behind it. The tool doesn't call this wrong, it has no way to know if the analyst had a real reason they just didn't write down. It only reports, accurately, that nothing was declared.

It isn't trying to merge two minds into one

So the comparison engine isn't trying to reconcile two investigators into a single answer. It's trying to make the relationship between their reasoning inspectable. It just asks smaller, more answerable questions: which evidence did only one analyst use? Where did confidence start to pull apart? Did two people reach the same conclusion by entirely different paths?

Those aren't answers. They're questions worth asking before a conclusion gets accepted as final. The goal isn't a verdict it's a shared language for disagreement, so it stops getting quietly absorbed into "well, we wrote two different reports."

Where this falls short, on purpose and by accident

Some of this is a real limitation I haven't solved; some of it is a boundary I drew on purpose and intend to keep. Match suggestions are lexical keyword overlap, nothing smarter a human reviewer has to confirm or reject every one. Structured entry is a genuine cost: breaking your own reasoning into typed pieces takes more effort than writing a paragraph, and I don't yet know if what it buys is worth what it costs. The five-part taxonomy might not fit how every investigator actually thinks.

The first draft of this, in my head, was much bigger — a graph canvas, real-time collaboration, permission tiers, an API, a database, export pipelines, dashboards. None of that answers the only question that matters right now: does comparing reasoning paths reveal useful differences a normal review misses? So I cut it down to exactly what's needed to test that, and nothing else.

A more detailed treatment covering prior art (SEAS, CISpaces, W3C PROV, argument mapping, structured analytic techniques), specific failure modes, the full data model, and the pilot protocol with predefined continuation and failure thresholds is in the repository under docs/research-assessment-v0.1.md.

The test

The next step is small on purpose: two analysts, one reviewer, three cases, one straightforward, one genuinely ambiguous with no single correct answer, one noisy and incomplete on purpose. Each case also gets reviewed the ordinary way, prose only, no structure, as the baseline this has to beat.

What gets measured: how long structured entry takes, how long review takes with the tool versus without it, how many reported differences a reviewer judges genuinely useful and non-obvious rather than just accurate, how many are misleading or simply wrong, what important differences the reviewer finds that the tool never surfaced at all, and whether anyone involved would choose to use it again.

None of those numbers exist yet. That's the entire point of running the test instead of writing more code.

This isn't about replacing investigators

The project is not intended to automate judgment or evaluate investigators. The most valuable part of an investigation is still the investigator: curiosity, experience, skepticism, pattern recognition, and the willingness to change direction when new evidence appears. A comparison engine cannot supply those things. If Reasoning Diff Lab succeeds, it will be because it made that judgment easier to inspect, discuss, and learn from not because it replaced it.

Maybe this is a terrible idea

Seriously. It might be. The reports may surface differences nobody actually cares about. The pilot may tell me I've spent months building an elegant answer to a question nobody was asking.

That's a real possibility.

But there's another one. Maybe disagreement isn't something to eliminate maybe it's something to inspect. Maybe the interesting artifact was never the final conclusion. Maybe it's the moment two careful people quietly stopped thinking the same way.

I don't know. That's why this exists. Not to prove the idea. To test it.

If it fails, I want to know why. If it succeeds, I want to know why. Either result is worth more than convincing myself it works from the inside.

I'm looking for pilot participants. If you investigate things for a living—incident response, intelligence, digital forensics, journalism, medicine, security research, or even debugging—and you're willing to run the included synthetic cases through this and tell me exactly where the workflow broke, wasted your time, or showed you something you would otherwise have missed, I want to hear from you.

The initial pilot requires two independent analysts and one reviewer, takes approximately 90 minutes, runs locally, and does not require participants to submit real investigative evidence.

Everything needed to inspect or run the pilot is available here:

  • Project repository and v2.0.0 release
  • Research assessment — prior art, failure modes, data model, and predefined continuation and failure thresholds
  • Pilot protocol
  • Facilitator packet

Comment below, open a GitHub issue, or reach out through my DEV profile. The next meaningful edit to this project should happen after real participants break, validate, or complicate the hypothesis—not before.

sentences.zh: 没有人会通过从头到尾阅读每个版本并牢记其中的差异来审查文件的两个版本。

sentences.en: A diff tool does that reconstruction for you, it doesn't tell you which version is better, it just shows you exactly where and how they parted ways.
sentences.zh: diff 工具可以为您进行重建，它不会告诉您哪个版本更好，它只是向您准确显示它们在哪里以及如何分道扬镳。

blocks.html_en: When two investigators disagree, we still tend to do it the old way: put both reports side by side and ask a third person to reconstruct where the thinking diverged. That reconstruction is slow, it's subjective, and it's usually incomplete, because neither analyst ever recorded their reasoning in a form that could actually be compared.

sentences.en: When two investigators disagree, we still tend to do it the old way: put both reports side by side and ask a third person to reconstruct where the thinking diverged.
sentences.zh: 当两位调查员意见不一致时，我们仍然倾向于采用老方法：将两份报告并排放置，然后请第三人重建思维分歧的地方。

sentences.en: That reconstruction is slow, it's subjective, and it's usually incomplete, because neither analyst ever recorded their reasoning in a form that could actually be compared.
sentences.zh: 这种重建是缓慢的、主观的，而且通常是不完整的，因为两位分析师都没有以可以实际比较的形式记录他们的推理。

blocks.html_en: This does not mean nobody has tried to structure or preserve reasoning before. Structured analytic techniques, argument-mapping systems, and analytic-provenance tools have been doing parts of this work for years. I could not find a practical workflow centered specifically on freezing two independently authored reasoning paths, asking a separate reviewer to align them, and preserving those alignment decisions as part of the resulting diff. That narrower combination is what Reasoning Diff Lab is testing. A full treatment of the prior art, SEAS, CISpaces, W3C PROV, argument mapping, and the analytic-provenance literature is in the research assessment linked at the end.

sentences.en: This does not mean nobody has tried to structure or preserve reasoning before.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着以前没有人尝试过构建或保留推理。

sentences.en: Structured analytic techniques, argument-mapping systems, and analytic-provenance tools have been doing parts of this work for years.
sentences.zh: 结构化分析技术、论证映射系统和分析来源工具多年来一直在完成这项工作的一部分。

sentences.en: I could not find a practical workflow centered specifically on freezing two independently authored reasoning paths, asking a separate reviewer to align them, and preserving those alignment decisions as part of the resulting diff.
sentences.zh: 我找不到一个实用的工作流程，专门专注于冻结两个独立编写的推理路径，要求单独的审阅者对齐它们，并将这些对齐决策保留为结果差异的一部分。

sentences.en: That narrower combination is what Reasoning Diff Lab is testing.
sentences.zh: Reasoning Diff Lab 正在测试这种更窄的组合。

sentences.en: A full treatment of the prior art, SEAS, CISpaces, W3C PROV, argument mapping, and the analytic-provenance literature is in the research assessment linked at the end.
sentences.zh: 最后链接的研究评估中对现有技术、SEAS、CISpaces、W3C PROV、论证映射和分析出处文献进行了全面处理。

blocks.html_en: So I built enough of an answer to find out whether the question was worth asking. I called it Reasoning Diff Lab.

sentences.en: So I built enough of an answer to find out whether the question was worth asking.
sentences.zh: 所以我建立了足够的答案来确定这个问题是否值得提出。

sentences.en: I called it Reasoning Diff Lab.
sentences.zh: 我将其称为推理差异实验室。

blocks.html_en: Status: pilot-ready, empirically unvalidated. The current v2.0.0 release includes the analyst-entry workflow, frozen path snapshots, reviewer alignment, deterministic comparison reports, and three synthetic cases. It passes 58 tests with 0 failures, and a full build produces 22 divergence events across those cases. That proves the instrument runs as designed. It does not prove that investigators will find it useful that is exactly what the pilot below is designed to determine.

sentences.en: Status: pilot-ready, empirically unvalidated.
sentences.zh: 状态：试点就绪，未经经验验证。

sentences.en: The current v2.0.0 release includes the analyst-entry workflow, frozen path snapshots, reviewer alignment, deterministic comparison reports, and three synthetic cases.
sentences.zh: 当前的 v2.0.0 版本包括分析师输入工作流程、冻结路径快照、审阅者对齐、确定性比较报告和三个综合案例。

sentences.en: It passes 58 tests with 0 failures, and a full build produces 22 divergence events across those cases.
sentences.zh: 它通过了 58 项测试，0 次失败，完整的构建在这些情况下产生了 22 个分歧事件。

sentences.en: That proves the instrument runs as designed.
sentences.zh: 这证明仪器按设计运行。

sentences.en: It does not prove that investigators will find it useful that is exactly what the pilot below is designed to determine.
sentences.zh: 它并不能证明调查人员会发现它有用，而这正是下面的试点旨在确定的。

blocks.html_en: What it actually is

sentences.en: What it actually is
sentences.zh: 它实际上是什么

blocks.html_en: It's a local-first research prototype that compares two independently produced reasoning paths against the same evidence set.

sentences.en: It's a local-first research prototype that compares two independently produced reasoning paths against the same evidence set.
sentences.zh: 这是一个本地优先的研究原型，将两个独立生成的推理路径与相同的证据集进行比较。

blocks.html_en: I want to be just as clear about what it doesn't do, because this is the part that matters most. It does not determine truth, rank investigators, or declare one analyst better than the other. It does not infer a contradiction from wording a contradiction only exists in its output if a human reviewer explicitly confirms one. It does not replace human review; it tries to make that review faster to start, and harder to skip a step in.

sentences.en: I want to be just as clear about what it doesn't do, because this is the part that matters most.
sentences.zh: 我想清楚地说明它不做什么，因为这是最重要的部分。

sentences.en: It does not determine truth, rank investigators, or declare one analyst better than the other.
sentences.zh: 它不能确定真相、对调查人员进行排名或宣布一位分析师比另一位分析师更好。

sentences.en: It does not infer a contradiction from wording a contradiction only exists in its output if a human reviewer explicitly confirms one.
sentences.zh: 它不会从措辞中推断出矛盾，只有当人类审阅者明确确认矛盾时，矛盾才存在于其输出中。

sentences.en: It does not replace human review; it tries to make that review faster to start, and harder to skip a step in.
sentences.zh: 它不会取代人工审查；它试图让审查更快地开始，并且更难跳过一步。

blocks.html_en: Each analyst breaks their reasoning into small typed pieces an observation, an assumption, an inference, a claim, an explicit unknown and tags which evidence and which earlier piece each one depends on, with a confidence level attached. A reviewer who authored neither path matches the two sets: same position, related but distinct, or unrelated. Contradiction is separate it must be declared by the reviewer and is never guessed by the system. From there, everything is mechanical: the tool walks the matched and unmatched pieces and reports what it finds. If the report says two analysts diverged, you can trace that line back to the exact evidence, the exact dependency chain, and the exact reviewer decision whose call it was, and what they chose that produced it.

sentences.en: Each analyst breaks their reasoning into small typed pieces an observation, an assumption, an inference, a claim, an explicit unknown and tags which evidence and which earlier piece each one depends on, with a confidence level attached.
sentences.zh: 每个分析师将他们的推理分解成小的打字片段：观察、假设、推论、主张、明确的未知数，并标记每个人依赖的证据和早期片段，并附加置信度。

sentences.en: A reviewer who authored neither path matches the two sets: same position, related but distinct, or unrelated.
sentences.zh: 创作这两条路径的审阅者与这两组匹配：位置相同、相关但不同或不相关。

sentences.en: Contradiction is separate it must be declared by the reviewer and is never guessed by the system.
sentences.zh: 矛盾是独立的，它必须由审阅者声明，并且系统永远不会猜测。

sentences.en: From there, everything is mechanical: the tool walks the matched and unmatched pieces and reports what it finds.
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，一切都是机械的：工具遍历匹配和不匹配的部分并报告它发现的内容。

sentences.en: If the report says two analysts diverged, you can trace that line back to the exact evidence, the exact dependency chain, and the exact reviewer decision whose call it was, and what they chose that produced it.
sentences.zh: 如果报告称两位分析师存在分歧，您可以追溯到确切的证据、确切的依赖链、确切的审阅者决定，以及他们选择的内容。

blocks.html_en: What it surfaces in practice:

sentences.en: What it surfaces in practice:
sentences.zh: 它在实践中表现出来的是什么：

blocks.html_en: • Shared evidence, different interpretation. Both analysts cite the same authentication log. One reads it as stolen credentials. The other reads it as expired-token behavior. Same source, materially different explanation.

sentences.en: Shared evidence, different interpretation.
sentences.zh: 共享证据，不同解释。

sentences.en: Both analysts cite the same authentication log.
sentences.zh: 两位分析师都引用了相同的身份验证日志。

sentences.en: One reads it as stolen credentials.
sentences.zh: 人们将其视为被盗的凭证。

sentences.en: The other reads it as expired-token behavior.
sentences.zh: 另一个将其视为过期令牌行为。

sentences.en: Same source, materially different explanation.
sentences.zh: 相同的来源，截然不同的解释。

blocks.html_en: • Evidence used by only one side. One analyst built part of their case on the deployment timeline. The other never touched it — maybe for a good reason, maybe because they never saw it.

sentences.en: Evidence used by only one side.
sentences.zh: 证据仅由一方使用。

sentences.en: One analyst built part of their case on the deployment timeline.
sentences.zh: 一位分析师根据部署时间表构建了他们的部分案例。

sentences.en: The other never touched it — maybe for a good reason, maybe because they never saw it.
sentences.zh: 另一个从未碰过它——也许是有充分的理由，也许是因为他们从未见过它。

blocks.html_en: • Confidence divergence. Two analysts land on the same conclusion. One is 90% sure. The other is 55%. That gap is invisible if all you ever compare is the final sentence.

sentences.en: Confidence divergence.
sentences.zh: 信心分歧。

sentences.en: Two analysts land on the same conclusion.
sentences.zh: 两位分析师得出了相同的结论。

sentences.en: One is 90% sure.
sentences.zh: 1.有90%的把握。

sentences.en: The other is 55%.
sentences.zh: 另一个是55%。

sentences.en: That gap is invisible if all you ever compare is the final sentence.
sentences.zh: 如果你比较的只是最后一句话，那么这种差距是看不见的。

blocks.html_en: • Undeclared support. A claim exists with no evidence and no stated reasoning behind it. The tool doesn't call this wrong, it has no way to know if the analyst had a real reason they just didn't write down. It only reports, accurately, that nothing was declared.

sentences.en: Undeclared support.
sentences.zh: 未声明的支持。

sentences.en: A claim exists with no evidence and no stated reasoning behind it.
sentences.zh: 一项主张的存在没有证据，也没有明确的推理依据。

sentences.en: The tool doesn't call this wrong, it has no way to know if the analyst had a real reason they just didn't write down.
sentences.zh: 该工具不会认为这是错误的，它无法知道分析师是否有他们没有写下来的真正原因。

sentences.en: It only reports, accurately, that nothing was declared.
sentences.zh: 它只是准确地报告没有宣布任何内容。

blocks.html_en: It isn't trying to merge two minds into one

sentences.en: It isn't trying to merge two minds into one
sentences.zh: 它并不是试图将两种思想合而为一

blocks.html_en: So the comparison engine isn't trying to reconcile two investigators into a single answer. It's trying to make the relationship between their reasoning inspectable. It just asks smaller, more answerable questions: which evidence did only one analyst use? Where did confidence start to pull apart? Did two people reach the same conclusion by entirely different paths?

sentences.en: So the comparison engine isn't trying to reconcile two investigators into a single answer.
sentences.zh: 因此，比较引擎并不是试图将两个调查员协调成一个答案。

sentences.en: It's trying to make the relationship between their reasoning inspectable.
sentences.zh: 它试图使他们的推理之间的关系变得可检查。

sentences.en: It just asks smaller, more answerable questions: which evidence did only one analyst use?
sentences.zh: 它只是提出更小、更容易回答的问题：只有一位分析师使用了哪些证据？

sentences.en: Where did confidence start to pull apart?
sentences.zh: 信心从哪里开始崩溃？

sentences.en: Did two people reach the same conclusion by entirely different paths?
sentences.zh: 两个人是否通过完全不同的路径得出了相同的结论？

blocks.html_en: Those aren't answers. They're questions worth asking before a conclusion gets accepted as final. The goal isn't a verdict it's a shared language for disagreement, so it stops getting quietly absorbed into "well, we wrote two different reports."

sentences.en: Those aren't answers.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是答案。

sentences.en: They're questions worth asking before a conclusion gets accepted as final.
sentences.zh: 在最终结论被接受之前，这些问题值得提出。

sentences.en: The goal isn't a verdict it's a shared language for disagreement, so it stops getting quietly absorbed into "well, we wrote two different reports."
sentences.zh: 我们的目标不是一个裁决，而是一种表达分歧的共同语言，因此它不再静静地陷入“好吧，我们写了两份不同的报告”。

blocks.html_en: Where this falls short, on purpose and by accident

sentences.en: Where this falls short, on purpose and by accident
sentences.zh: 有意或无意的不足之处

blocks.html_en: Some of this is a real limitation I haven't solved; some of it is a boundary I drew on purpose and intend to keep. Match suggestions are lexical keyword overlap, nothing smarter a human reviewer has to confirm or reject every one. Structured entry is a genuine cost: breaking your own reasoning into typed pieces takes more effort than writing a paragraph, and I don't yet know if what it buys is worth what it costs. The five-part taxonomy might not fit how every investigator actually thinks.

sentences.en: Some of this is a real limitation I haven't solved; some of it is a boundary I drew on purpose and intend to keep.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是我尚未解决的真正限制；其中一些是我故意划定并打算保留的界限。

sentences.en: Match suggestions are lexical keyword overlap, nothing smarter a human reviewer has to confirm or reject every one.
sentences.zh: 匹配建议是词汇关键字重叠，人类审阅者无需更聪明地确认或拒绝每一个建议。

sentences.en: Structured entry is a genuine cost: breaking your own reasoning into typed pieces takes more effort than writing a paragraph, and I don't yet know if what it buys is worth what it costs.
sentences.zh: 结构化输入是一项真正的成本：将自己的推理分解成打印的片段比写一个段落需要更多的努力，而且我还不知道它所购买的东西是否值得它花费的成本。

sentences.en: The five-part taxonomy might not fit how every investigator actually thinks.
sentences.zh: 由五部分组成的分类法可能并不符合每个调查人员的实际想法。

blocks.html_en: The first draft of this, in my head, was much bigger — a graph canvas, real-time collaboration, permission tiers, an API, a database, export pipelines, dashboards. None of that answers the only question that matters right now: does comparing reasoning paths reveal useful differences a normal review misses? So I cut it down to exactly what's needed to test that, and nothing else.

sentences.en: The first draft of this, in my head, was much bigger — a graph canvas, real-time collaboration, permission tiers, an API, a database, export pipelines, dashboards.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这个初稿要大得多——图表画布、实时协作、权限层、API、数据库、导出管道、仪表板。

sentences.en: None of that answers the only question that matters right now: does comparing reasoning paths reveal useful differences a normal review misses?
sentences.zh: 这些都不能回答目前唯一重要的问题：比较推理路径是否揭示了正常审查所遗漏的有用差异？

sentences.en: So I cut it down to exactly what's needed to test that, and nothing else.
sentences.zh: 因此，我将其缩减为测试所需的内容，仅此而已。

blocks.html_en: A more detailed treatment covering prior art (SEAS, CISpaces, W3C PROV, argument mapping, structured analytic techniques), specific failure modes, the full data model, and the pilot protocol with predefined continuation and failure thresholds is in the repository under docs/research-assessment-v0.1.md.

sentences.en: A more detailed treatment covering prior art (SEAS, CISpaces, W3C PROV, argument mapping, structured analytic techniques), specific failure modes, the full data model, and the pilot protocol with predefined continuation and failure thresholds is in the repository under docs/research-assessment-v0.1.md.
sentences.zh: 更详细的处理涵盖现有技术（SEAS、CISpaces、W3C PROV、参数映射、结构化分析技术）、特定故障模式、完整数据模型以及具有预定义的延续和故障阈值的试点协议，位于 docs/research-assessment-v0.1.md 下的存储库中。

blocks.html_en: The test

sentences.en: The test
sentences.zh: 测试

blocks.html_en: The next step is small on purpose: two analysts, one reviewer, three cases, one straightforward, one genuinely ambiguous with no single correct answer, one noisy and incomplete on purpose. Each case also gets reviewed the ordinary way, prose only, no structure, as the baseline this has to beat.

sentences.en: The next step is small on purpose: two analysts, one reviewer, three cases, one straightforward, one genuinely ambiguous with no single correct answer, one noisy and incomplete on purpose.
sentences.zh: 下一步故意做得很小：两名分析师，一名审稿人，三个案例，一个是直截了当的，一个是真正模棱两可的，没有一个正确的答案，一个是故意吵闹且不完整的。

sentences.en: Each case also gets reviewed the ordinary way, prose only, no structure, as the baseline this has to beat.
sentences.zh: 每个案例也都以普通的方式进行审查，只有散文，没有结构，作为必须超越的基线。

blocks.html_en: What gets measured: how long structured entry takes, how long review takes with the tool versus without it, how many reported differences a reviewer judges genuinely useful and non-obvious rather than just accurate, how many are misleading or simply wrong, what important differences the reviewer finds that the tool never surfaced at all, and whether anyone involved would choose to use it again.

sentences.en: What gets measured: how long structured entry takes, how long review takes with the tool versus without it, how many reported differences a reviewer judges genuinely useful and non-obvious rather than just accurate, how many are misleading or simply wrong, what important differences the reviewer finds that the tool never surfaced at all, and whether anyone involved would choose to use it again.
sentences.zh: 衡量的内容：结构化输入需要多长时间，使用该工具与不使用该工具的审核需要多长时间，审核者认为有多少报告的差异是真正有用和不明显的，而不仅仅是准确的，有多少是误导性的或完全错误的，审核者发现该工具根本没有出现过的重要差异有哪些，以及相关人员是否会选择再次使用它。

blocks.html_en: None of those numbers exist yet. That's the entire point of running the test instead of writing more code.

sentences.en: None of those numbers exist yet.
sentences.zh: 这些数字目前还不存在。

sentences.en: That's the entire point of running the test instead of writing more code.
sentences.zh: 这就是运行测试而不是编写更多代码的全部意义。

blocks.html_en: This isn't about replacing investigators

sentences.en: This isn't about replacing investigators
sentences.zh: 这并不是要更换调查员

blocks.html_en: The project is not intended to automate judgment or evaluate investigators. The most valuable part of an investigation is still the investigator: curiosity, experience, skepticism, pattern recognition, and the willingness to change direction when new evidence appears. A comparison engine cannot supply those things. If Reasoning Diff Lab succeeds, it will be because it made that judgment easier to inspect, discuss, and learn from not because it replaced it.

sentences.en: The project is not intended to automate judgment or evaluate investigators.
sentences.zh: 该项目并非旨在自动判断或评估调查人员。

sentences.en: The most valuable part of an investigation is still the investigator: curiosity, experience, skepticism, pattern recognition, and the willingness to change direction when new evidence appears.
sentences.zh: 调查中最有价值的部分仍然是调查员：好奇心、经验、怀疑精神、模式识别以及在新证据出现时改变方向的意愿。

sentences.en: A comparison engine cannot supply those things.
sentences.zh: 比较引擎无法提供这些东西。

sentences.en: If Reasoning Diff Lab succeeds, it will be because it made that judgment easier to inspect, discuss, and learn from not because it replaced it.
sentences.zh: 如果推理差异实验室成功，那将是因为它使该判断更容易检查、讨论和学习，而不是因为它取代了它。

blocks.html_en: Maybe this is a terrible idea

sentences.en: Maybe this is a terrible idea
sentences.zh: 也许这是一个糟糕的主意

blocks.html_en: Seriously. It might be. The reports may surface differences nobody actually cares about. The pilot may tell me I've spent months building an elegant answer to a question nobody was asking.

sentences.en: Seriously.
sentences.zh: 严重地。

sentences.en: It might be.
sentences.zh: 可能是这样。

sentences.en: The reports may surface differences nobody actually cares about.
sentences.zh: 这些报告可能会暴露出没有人真正关心的差异。

sentences.en: The pilot may tell me I've spent months building an elegant answer to a question nobody was asking.
sentences.zh: 飞行员可能会告诉我，我花了几个月的时间为一个没有人问的问题找到一个优雅的答案。

blocks.html_en: That's a real possibility.

sentences.en: That's a real possibility.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的可能性。

blocks.html_en: But there's another one. Maybe disagreement isn't something to eliminate maybe it's something to inspect. Maybe the interesting artifact was never the final conclusion. Maybe it's the moment two careful people quietly stopped thinking the same way.

sentences.en: But there's another one.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一种。

sentences.en: Maybe disagreement isn't something to eliminate maybe it's something to inspect.
sentences.zh: 也许分歧不是要消除的东西，也许是需要检查的东西。

sentences.en: Maybe the interesting artifact was never the final conclusion.
sentences.zh: 也许有趣的文物从来都不是最终的结论。

sentences.en: Maybe it's the moment two careful people quietly stopped thinking the same way.
sentences.zh: 也许就在这一刻，两个细心的人悄悄地不再以同样的方式思考。

blocks.html_en: I don't know. That's why this exists. Not to prove the idea. To test it.

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: That's why this exists.
sentences.zh: 这就是它存在的原因。

sentences.en: Not to prove the idea.
sentences.zh: 不是为了证明这个想法。

sentences.en: To test it.
sentences.zh: 来测试一下。

blocks.html_en: If it fails, I want to know why. If it succeeds, I want to know why. Either result is worth more than convincing myself it works from the inside.

sentences.en: If it fails, I want to know why.
sentences.zh: 如果失败了，我想知道原因。

sentences.en: If it succeeds, I want to know why.
sentences.zh: 如果成功的话，我想知道为什么。

sentences.en: Either result is worth more than convincing myself it works from the inside.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种结果都比说服自己它从内部起作用更有价值。

blocks.html_en: I'm looking for pilot participants. If you investigate things for a living—incident response, intelligence, digital forensics, journalism, medicine, security research, or even debugging—and you're willing to run the included synthetic cases through this and tell me exactly where the workflow broke, wasted your time, or showed you something you would otherwise have missed, I want to hear from you.

content_html_zh:
每项调查最终都会到达同一时刻。

两个有能力的人看到相同的证据后却相信不同的事情。

这并不罕见。 不寻常的是接下来发生的事情。 我们比较他们的结论。 不是他们的推理。 我们争论谁是对的。 我们几乎从不问他们从哪里开始有不同的想法。

这让我觉得倒退了。

我们存档证据。 我们很少存档推理。

每次调查都会留下文物。 日志。 磁盘映像。 照片。 证人陈述。 源代码。 这些文物成为永久记录的一部分，被索引、散列并保存多年。

具有讽刺意味的是，将它们联系起来的推理通常会消失。 一路上所做的假设。 被考虑并被拒绝的替代解释。 某人的信心在那一刻发生了变化。 这些事情通常只存在于记忆中、零散的笔记中，或者根本没有被记录下来的对话中。

几周后，审查调查的人可能掌握了原始调查人员掌握的所有证据，但几乎没有任何分析路径使这些证据有意义。 当出现分歧时，我们会在事后重建推理，而不是检查发生时记录的推理。

我开始想知道这个缺失的文物——推理本身是否值得保留。 不是因为它决定了真相。 因为它解释了如何追求真理。

我们很好地保存了证据。 我们的推理能力非常差。

每个调查员都会留下指纹

每个调查员都会养成习惯。 不是坏习惯，而是思维习惯。

有些人首先制定时间表，然后再做其他事情。 有些人本能地不相信时间表，因为时钟会漂移，没有人仔细检查它们。 有些人不断地问：“什么证据会改变我的想法？” 其他人问：“什么解释了最多的观察结果？” 一些调查人员自然会对来源表示怀疑，直到它经过反复审查。 其他人则天生具有生成性——他们快速建立一个假设，并在剩下的调查中试图打破它。

这两种方法都没有错。 他们是不同的。 这正是调查受益于多个独立人员参与的原因。 如果每个人都遵循完全相同的过程，他们可能会错过完全相同的盲点。 独立思考并不是需要消除的噪音。 这是要保存的信息。

问题从来不在于调查人员的想法不同。 问题是我们通常会丢弃他们的不同想法的记录。 当调查写成时，大部分路径已经消失在精美的叙述中。 报告会告诉您他们到达的地点。 它很少告诉你他们走了哪条路线。

我开始想知道这条路线是否真的是有趣的部分。

如果我们可以像 Git 比较代码那样进行比较推理会怎么样？

没有人会通过从头到尾阅读每个版本并牢记其中的差异来审查文件的两个版本。 diff 工具可以为您进行重建，它不会告诉您哪个版本更好，它只是向您准确显示它们在哪里以及如何分道扬镳。

当两位调查员意见不一致时，我们仍然倾向于采用老方法：将两份报告并排放置，然后请第三人重建思维分歧的地方。 这种重建是缓慢的、主观的，而且通常是不完整的，因为两位分析师都没有以可以实际比较的形式记录他们的推理。

这并不意味着以前没有人尝试过构建或保留推理。 结构化分析技术、论证映射系统和分析来源工具多年来一直在完成这项工作的一部分。 我找不到一个实用的工作流程，专门专注于冻结两个独立编写的推理路径，要求单独的审阅者对齐它们，并将这些对齐决策保留为结果差异的一部分。 Reasoning Diff Lab 正在测试这种更窄的组合。 最后链接的研究评估中对现有技术、SEAS、CISpaces、W3C PROV、论证映射和分析出处文献进行了全面处理。

所以我建立了足够的答案来确定这个问题是否值得提出。 我将其称为推理差异实验室。

状态：试点就绪，未经经验验证。 当前的 v2.0.0 版本包括分析师输入工作流程、冻结路径快照、审阅者对齐、确定性比较报告和三个综合案例。 它通过了 58 项测试，0 次失败，完整的构建在这些情况下产生了 22 个分歧事件。 这证明仪器按设计运行。 它并不能证明调查人员会发现它有用，而这正是下面的试点旨在确定的。

它实际上是什么

这是一个本地优先的研究原型，将两个独立生成的推理路径与相同的证据集进行比较。

我想清楚地说明它不做什么，因为这是最重要的部分。 它不能确定真相、对调查人员进行排名或宣布一位分析师比另一位分析师更好。 它不会从措辞中推断出矛盾，只有当人类审阅者明确确认矛盾时，矛盾才存在于其输出中。 它不会取代人工审查；它试图让审查更快地开始，并且更难跳过一步。

每个分析师将他们的推理分解成小的打字片段：观察、假设、推论、主张、明确的未知数，并标记每个人依赖的证据和早期片段，并附加置信度。 创作这两条路径的审阅者与这两组匹配：位置相同、相关但不同或不相关。 矛盾是独立的，它必须由审阅者声明，并且系统永远不会猜测。 从那里开始，一切都是机械的：工具遍历匹配和不匹配的部分并报告它发现的内容。 如果报告称两位分析师存在分歧，您可以追溯到确切的证据、确切的依赖链、确切的审阅者决定，以及他们选择的内容。

它在实践中表现出来的是什么：

  • 共享证据，不同解释。 两位分析师都引用了相同的身份验证日志。 人们将其视为被盗的凭证。 另一个将其视为过期令牌行为。 相同的来源，截然不同的解释。
  • 证据仅由一方使用。 一位分析师根据部署时间表构建了他们的部分案例。 另一个从未碰过它——也许是有充分的理由，也许是因为他们从未见过它。
  • 信心分歧。 两位分析师得出了相同的结论。 1.有90%的把握。 另一个是55%。 如果你比较的只是最后一句话，那么这种差距是看不见的。
  • 未声明的支持。 一项主张的存在没有证据，也没有明确的推理依据。 该工具不会认为这是错误的，它无法知道分析师是否有他们没有写下来的真正原因。 它只是准确地报告没有宣布任何内容。

它并不是试图将两种思想合而为一

因此，比较引擎并不是试图将两个调查员协调成一个答案。 它试图使他们的推理之间的关系变得可检查。 它只是提出更小、更容易回答的问题：只有一位分析师使用了哪些证据？ 信心从哪里开始崩溃？ 两个人是否通过完全不同的路径得出了相同的结论？

这些都不是答案。 在最终结论被接受之前，这些问题值得提出。 我们的目标不是一个裁决，而是一种表达分歧的共同语言，因此它不再静静地陷入“好吧，我们写了两份不同的报告”。

有意或无意的不足之处

其中一些是我尚未解决的真正限制；其中一些是我故意划定并打算保留的界限。 匹配建议是词汇关键字重叠，人类审阅者无需更聪明地确认或拒绝每一个建议。 结构化输入是一项真正的成本：将自己的推理分解成打印的片段比写一个段落需要更多的努力，而且我还不知道它所购买的东西是否值得它花费的成本。 由五部分组成的分类法可能并不符合每个调查人员的实际想法。

在我看来，这个初稿要大得多——图表画布、实时协作、权限层、API、数据库、导出管道、仪表板。 这些都不能回答目前唯一重要的问题：比较推理路径是否揭示了正常审查所遗漏的有用差异？ 因此，我将其缩减为测试所需的内容，仅此而已。

更详细的处理涵盖现有技术（SEAS、CISpaces、W3C PROV、参数映射、结构化分析技术）、特定故障模式、完整数据模型以及具有预定义的延续和故障阈值的试点协议，位于 docs/research-assessment-v0.1.md 下的存储库中。

测试

下一步故意做得很小：两名分析师，一名审稿人，三个案例，一个是直截了当的，一个是真正模棱两可的，没有一个正确的答案，一个是故意吵闹且不完整的。 每个案例也都以普通的方式进行审查，只有散文，没有结构，作为必须超越的基线。

衡量的内容：结构化输入需要多长时间，使用该工具与不使用该工具的审核需要多长时间，审核者认为有多少报告的差异是真正有用和不明显的，而不仅仅是准确的，有多少是误导性的或完全错误的，审核者发现该工具根本没有出现过的重要差异有哪些，以及相关人员是否会选择再次使用它。

这些数字目前还不存在。 这就是运行测试而不是编写更多代码的全部意义。

这并不是要更换调查员

该项目并非旨在自动判断或评估调查人员。 调查中最有价值的部分仍然是调查员：好奇心、经验、怀疑精神、模式识别以及在新证据出现时改变方向的意愿。 比较引擎无法提供这些东西。 如果推理差异实验室成功，那将是因为它使该判断更容易检查、讨论和学习，而不是因为它取代了它。

也许这是一个糟糕的主意

严重地。 可能是这样。 这些报告可能会暴露出没有人真正关心的差异。 飞行员可能会告诉我，我花了几个月的时间为一个没有人问的问题找到一个优雅的答案。

这是一个真正的可能性。

但还有另一种。 也许分歧不是要消除的东西，也许是需要检查的东西。 也许有趣的文物从来都不是最终的结论。 也许就在这一刻，两个细心的人悄悄地不再以同样的方式思考。

我不知道。 这就是它存在的原因。 不是为了证明这个想法。 来测试一下。

如果失败了，我想知道原因。 如果成功的话，我想知道为什么。 无论哪种结果都比说服自己它从内部起作用更有价值。

我正在寻找试点参与者。 如果您以调查事物为生——事件响应、情报、数字取证、新闻、医学、安全研究，甚至调试——并且您愿意通过此运行所包含的综合案例，并准确地告诉我工作流程在哪里中断、浪费了您的时间，或者向您展示了您可能会错过的东西，我希望收到您的来信。

最初的试点需要两名独立分析师和一名审核员，需要大约 90 分钟，在本地运行，并且不需要参与者提交真实的调查证据。

检查或运行试点所需的一切都可以在这里找到：

  • 项目存储库和 v2.0.0 版本
  • 研究评估——现有技术、故障模式、数据模型以及预定义的延续和故障阈值
  • 试点协议
  • 辅导员资料包

在下面发表评论、打开 GitHub 问题或通过我的 DEV 个人资料进行联系。 对这个项目的下一次有意义的编辑应该发生在真正的参与者打破、验证或复杂化假设之后——而不是之前。

证据告诉我们发生了什么。 推理告诉我们为什么相信它。 我们把第一个保存得非常好。 我感兴趣的是我们是否应该开始保留第二个。
